item.title: ‘Midwinter Break’ Review: Lesley Manville and Ciarán Hinds Go on One of the Most Depressing Movie Vacations Since Antonioni Made Them a Thing
item.description: To other movies like "L'avventura" and "La Notte" where couples wander new terrain while feeling like tourists in their own lives, director Polly Findlay says, "Hold my Guinness."

item.title: ‘The Perfect Neighbor’ Is Coming for That Best Documentary Oscar
item.description: Former editor Geeta Gandbhir tells IndieWire that her obsessive need to create a timeline for her grieving relatives opened up a new way to make a documentary.

item.title: Mike Leigh, Adam McKay, Tilda Swinton, and More Berlin Alumni Sign Open Letter Denouncing Fest’s ‘Silence’ and ‘Censoring’ on Gaza
item.description: After a fraught opening week and one lengthy statement from fest head Tricia Tuttle, the Berlinale is continuing to draw ire from those closest to it.

item.title: Richard Baneham and Eric Saindon on the ‘Never Easy’ Visual Effects of ‘Avatar: Fire and Ash’
item.description: Visual effects supervisor Baneham and Wētā FX senior effects supervisor Eric Saindon talk to IndieWire's Filmmaker Toolkit podcast about working on James Cameron's 197-minute epic — that has only seven seconds with no visual effects.

item.title: Oscar-Nominated ‘It Was Just an Accident’ Co-Screenwriter Mehdi Mahmoudian Has Been Released from Iranian Prison
item.description: Over the weekend, Jafar Panahi told IndieWire why his co-writer Mahmoudian was imprisoned, and why the director will return to Iran after the Oscars on March 15.

item.title: ‘Rose’ Review: A Gender-Bending Sandra Hüller Astounds in a 17th-Century Historical Fiction Knockout of Devastating Power
item.description: Berlin: Is Markus Schleinzer's rigorously controlled tale of a German woman who disguises herself as a male soldier the year's first full-out masterpiece? Maybe, baby.

item.title: ‘My Wife Cries’ Review: Angela Schanelec’s Marriage Story Is a Moving, Mysterious Humanist Marvel
item.description: Berlin: The German auteur painstakingly fashions a tapestry of lost time.

item.title: The Spirit Awards No Longer Define Independent Film. And That’s the Point
item.description: The ceremony hasn’t lost relevance, but it’s lost its monopoly in an industry that no longer organizes itself around any single room.

item.title: Will Warner Bros. Discovery Opening Up Merger Talks Again Finally Bring Some Clarity to the Paramount vs. Netflix Back and Forth?
item.description: Netflix is agreeing to give Paramount a 7-day window to lay its cards on the table. Will it finally bring an end to the saga?

item.title: ‘Wuthering Heights’ Puts Emerald Fennell in the Conversation for Highest-Grossing Female Directors
item.description: Though she's got a ways to go to catch Greta Gerwig, an $88.5 million opening weekend gross globally shows the auteur can deliver a hit.
